question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[2,3]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)={x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-6y+13. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[3,\,2]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[2.25,\,1.5]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$1.417$

current_example.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[1,2] \times [1,2] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2,$ where

$$
f(x,y) = x^3+y^3-3x-6y+9.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at $\mathbf x_0 = \big[1, \: 2 \big]^T$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives $\mathbf x_1 = \big[1, \: 1.5 \big]^T.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**
current_example.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is

$$
\mathbf{x}_{n+1} = \mathbf{x}_n - [H_f(\mathbf{x}_n)]^{-1} \nabla{f}(\mathbf{x}_n),
$$

where $H(\mathbf{x}_n)$ and $\nabla{f}(\mathbf{x}_n)$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at $\mathbf{x}_n.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3x-6y+9) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}-3x-6y+9)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-3 \\ 3{y}^{2}-6\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-3) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-6) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x & 0 \\ 0 & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14249685/assets/5868446402167c1a49b25451189e847ae7f7c609829a123b74b88f2eaa5f2a36.svg)

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}6x & 0 \\ 0 & 6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-3 \\ 3{y}^{2}-6\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6(1) & 0 \\ 0 & 6(1.5)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}-3 \\ 3(1.5)^{2}-6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0.75\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{6\cdot 9-0\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0.75\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{54}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4.5\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1.417\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
